value.hook: Open when a delivery looks downgraded, held or refused: read the store and the extension log before touching code
value.title: Evidence first: store queries that settled F116, F120, F113 and F124

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Four reported delivery bugs on 2026-11-08 had four different real causes. The store told which within minutes; the code would have misled.
- F116/F120 "downgraded to fyi-ride-along": no downgrade. The label marked a NORMAL message queued as the carrier of held FYIs. Proof: for every delivery.outcome reason X, find the next outcome for the same msg_id and seat; all 381 were delivered/injected within 5 s. Then check the holder's seat.activity flipping to working. Fixed in #173 (receipt wording, no time promise).
- F113 "steering held on GPT seats": rollout timing. held_deliveries join jobs gives where the time went (claimed_at - enqueued_at vs acked_at - claimed_at). seat.put payloads carry extension_build, so check which build each seat ran during the hold. All holds were on the pre-C31 build. #175 adds a stale-extension digest flag comparing extension source TREES (not commits).
- F124 "lease lapsed while working": the old extension's ~/.copilot/logs/process-<ts>-<pid>.log (the one that stops at the reload) showed receiver-rebaselined then receive-held "cannot prove discarded consumption", retryMs null. probeReceiver sets discardUncertain on any tail gap, and canRetryDiscarded then throws, so the receiver holds forever: no claims, no heartbeat, lease lapse, refusals. The steered message had in fact been consumed. The fix is still owed (handover-pij-swift-kestrel-2026-11-08.md). Also, delivery.outcome "transport" is always the daemon transport name (claude-uds) via publish_outcome, even on native-receiver refusals.
Recipes: sqlite3 -readonly ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite; jobs times are seconds and spine_events.at is ms; role_requests has fyi and reply; held_deliveries(job_id, recipient, flagged_at).
